verses.text: The apostles and the believers all through Judea heard that the Gentiles had also accepted God's word.
So when Peter went up to Jerusalem, the Jewish believers who held to circumcision argued with him.
They said, "You went into the house of men who are not circumcised, and you ate with them!"
So Peter began to explain to them step by step what had happened.
He said, "I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision. Something like a large sheet was being let down from heaven by its four corners, and it came down to where I was.
I looked closely at it and saw four-footed animals, wild animals, reptiles, and birds.
Then I heard a voice telling me, 'Get up, Peter. Kill and eat.'
I answered, 'Surely not, Lord! Nothing impure or unclean has ever entered my mouth.'
The voice spoke from heaven a second time: 'Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.'
This happened three times, and then it was all pulled back up to heaven.
Right then three men who had been sent to me from Caesarea stopped at the house where I was staying.
The Spirit told me to go with them and not to think of them as different. These six brothers also went with me, and we went into the man's house.
He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house. The angel said, 'Send to Joppa for Simon, who is called Peter.
He will bring you a message through which you and all your family will be saved.'
As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit came on them, just as he came on us at the beginning.
Then I remembered what the Lord had said: 'John baptised with water, but you will be baptised with the Holy Spirit.'
So if God gave them the same gift he gave us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to stand in God's way?"
When they heard this, they had nothing more to say. They praised God and said, "So then, God has given even the Gentiles the chance to turn from sin and receive life."
The believers who had been scattered by the attacks that began when Stephen was killed travelled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch. They told the message only to Jews.
But some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, went to Antioch and began to speak to Greeks too, telling them the good news about the Lord Jesus.
The Lord's power was with them, and a large number of people believed and turned to the Lord.
News of this reached the church in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
When he arrived and saw what God's grace had done, he was glad. He encouraged them all to stay true to the Lord with all their hearts.
Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith, and a great number of people were brought to the Lord.
Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul.

When he found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year Barnabas and Saul met with the church and taught large numbers of people. It was in Antioch that the followers were first called Christians.
During this time some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of them, named Agabus, stood up and through the Spirit said that a great famine would spread over the whole world. This happened while Claudius was emperor.
The followers decided that each of them would send help to the believers living in Judea, as much as each one was able.
They did this, sending their gift to the elders through Barnabas and Saul.
